parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Part of the name or of the e-mail, without telling case or accents apart.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Part of the name or of the e-mail, without telling case or accents apart.

parameters.name: managers
parameters.description: Only the Administrators and the Project managers, who may manage a project.

parameters.name: techLeads
parameters.description: Only the Administrators and the Tech leads, who may lead a project technically.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many people at most, from 1 to 100.

get.description: The tickets, tasks and requests of acceptance of the person by urgency: late, waiting for the person, due up to the next business day and in the next 7 days, in the views for me, opened by me and followed.

parameters.name: actorId
parameters.description: Only the records made by this user.

parameters.name: itemType
parameters.description: Only the records of this item type, such as User or SignIn.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start of the period, included.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End of the period, excluded.

post.description: Every record of the filter, newest first, for the spreadsheet of the audit; the export becomes a record of the audit (ADR-0099).

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Part of the name, without telling case or accents apart, or of the CNPJ, with or without punctuation.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Part of the code or of the name, without telling case or accents apart.

parameters.name: clientId
parameters.description: Only the projects of this client.

parameters.name: situation
parameters.description: Active (the default), Closed (completed and cancelled) or All.

parameters.name: mine
parameters.description: Only the projects the person is in, even for the Administrator.

get.description: The first 10 milestones not reached, from today on, of the open projects the person is in (ADR-0096).
What completing or cancelling the project would leave behind (ADR-0043), for who changes its status.
The numbers, the timeline, what needs attention and the team of the project (ADR-0073).

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: All (the default), AssignedToMe, UnassignedInMyTeams, Unassigned, OpenedByMe, Following or WithVendor.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Only the tickets of this project.

parameters.name: team
parameters.description: Only the tickets of this team.

parameters.name: situation
parameters.description: Open (the default: not resolved nor closed), Finished (resolved and closed) or All.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: The number, with or without #, or part of the title or of the description, without telling case or accents apart.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Priority (the default, the oldest first in each) or Number.

parameters.name: descending
parameters.description: From the highest priority or number to the lowest (the default).

parameters.name: personId
parameters.description: Only the tickets of which this person is the assignee or the requester.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Only the tickets of this project.

get.description: The active vendors, for new registrations of tickets at vendors (ADR-0028).
The people who may be the assignee of all the tickets of the numbers (ADR-0068).
The people who may be the requester of all the tickets of the numbers (ADR-0027).
All the attachments of the ticket in a .zip, in the order they were sent (Chamados-2.1).
The notifications of the person, the newest first, 30 at a time; with unread, only the ones not read.

post.description: Puts in the queue an e-mail to the Administrator, sent in the background.

AcceptanceActionsResponse.description: What the person may do with the term now.

AcceptanceCountsResponse.description: How many terms of each status the person sees.

AcceptanceDetailsResponse.description: A term with the message, the term to sign, the signed term, the reason of the refusal and the history.

AcceptanceEventKind.description: What happened to a term, for its history (ADR-0095).

AcceptanceEventResponse.description: An event of the history: what happened, who did it and when.

AcceptanceFileResponse.description: A file of a term: the name and the size.

AcceptanceListResponse.description:
The terms the person sees, the counts, whether the person sees every term of the project (who manages them) and
whether the person asks for and attaches terms now, which a closed project does not let.

AcceptanceMilestoneResponse.description: A milestone of the schedule with its current name, its day and the day it was reached.

AcceptanceRefusalRequest.description: The reason why the person refuses the term.

AcceptanceResponse.description:
A term of a list: the title, the status, the milestone (null when it left the schedule), the person of the term, who
asked and when (who attached it, for a term without a request), who answered and when, and whether it was asked for
in the system.

AcceptanceSignedResponse.description: The document of the signed term in the folder of the terms, opened by the documents.

AcceptanceStatus.description: Where a term stands (ADR-0035): waiting for the answer, signed, or refused with a reason.

AddLocalHolidayRequest.description: A new local holiday: the name, the date and whether it repeats every year.

AuditAction.description: What an audit record says happened.

AuditActorResponse.description: Who did it; null on the record means the system.

detail.description: The identity provider of a sign-in, or why a sign-in was refused.

AuditEntryResponse.description: One record of the Audit screen.

from.description: First day of the period, included.

to.description: Last day of the period, included; up to 366 days after the first.

itemType.description: Only the records of this item type, such as User or SignIn.

actorId.description: Only the records made by this user.

AuditExportRequest.description: What to export of the audit (ADR-0099): the days of the period in the time zone of the installation, both included.

AuditFieldResponse.description:
A changed field: the value before and after as invariant text, or none for a secret. A field that points to another
item, of the type in Reference (such as User), comes with the item's current name, or none when
the item no longer exists (ADR-0084).

CalculatedHolidayChoiceRequest.description: Whether a calculated holiday is considered, in every year.

CalendarDayKind.description: The kinds of dates of the calendar.

CalendarYearResponse.description:
The calendar of a year: the working days, from Monday to Sunday, and the dates in order. A calculated holiday has
its key (the screen names it); a local holiday has its id and name.

ChangeLocalHolidayRequest.description: A local holiday as a whole: the name, the date, the repetition and whether it is considered.

ChooseDailySummaryRequest.description: Whether the person receives the daily summary of e-mails (ADR-0037).

ClientChoiceResponse.description: A client to choose for a project or to filter the projects, without the CNPJ nor the observation.

ClientRequest.description: The client form: the name, the CNPJ with or without punctuation (empty for none) and the observation.

ClientResponse.description:
One client in the list: the CNPJ without punctuation (the screen formats it) and the address of the logo, which
changes whenever the logo changes, so the browser may keep it; null without a logo.

timelineLicense.description: The Syncfusion license key (ADR-0051, ADR-0087); none when not configured.

ClientSettingsResponse.description: What the browser needs from the configuration of the installation: the license key of the timeline.

ConsiderHolidaysRequest.description: Many dates considered or disregarded at once: the keys of calculated holidays and the ids of local ones.

CredentialImportRequest.description: The credentials to include from the spreadsheet: the lines the person marked, already mapped.

CredentialListResponse.description:
The credentials found, without the passwords; the environments of the project with how many credentials each has;
the total for the tab; and what the person may do.

CredentialPasswordResponse.description: The password of a credential, asked for showing or copying it.

CredentialPermissionsResponse.description: What the person may do with the credentials; all false in a completed or cancelled project.

CredentialRequest.description: A credential as the person fills it in; the password empty keeps the one a credential has.

CredentialResponse.description: A credential of the project, without the password: the portal, the environment, the address, the user and the notes.

DefaultFolderResponse.description: A default folder: the name, whether it is the folder of the acceptance terms, and whether it is active.

DocumentActionResponse.description: A person and when the person did something.

DocumentDetailsResponse.description: A document with its versions, newest first, and what the person may do with it.

DocumentFolderResponse.description: A folder of the project with how many documents not obsolete it has.

DocumentFoldersResponse.description: The folders the person sees, the total for the tab, the permissions and the size a file may have.

DocumentLinkRequest.description: The phase, or the task or milestone, the document is linked to; both null take the link away.

DocumentLinkResponse.description: The item of the schedule a document is linked to, with its current name.

DocumentPermissionsResponse.description: What the person may do with the documents of the project; all false in a completed or cancelled project.

DocumentResponse.description:
A document of a list: the folder, the status with who changed it and when, the current version with its size and
who sent it, and the link with the schedule.

DocumentStatus.description: Where a document stands, set by hand (ADR-0031); the obsolete ones leave the list by default.

EmailStatusResponse.description: The shared mailbox the e-mails leave from (null while none is configured) and the last test of the sending.

EmailTestQueuedResponse.description: The test e-mail is in the queue, to this address.

EmailTestResponse.description: The last test of the sending: where it stands, when and to whom (null once the queue forgot it).

EnvironmentCountResponse.description: An environment the credentials of the project use, with how many credentials it has.

GeneralRulesResponse.description:
The rules of the installation for the screens: the IANA time zone of dates and times (ADR-0013) and the time of the
daily summary of e-mails, in that time zone (ADR-0037), and how many days the notifications are kept (ADR-0038).

ImportedCredentialRequest.description: A credential mapped from a line of the spreadsheet, with the number of the line.

InstallationResponse.description:
The brand of the installation: the name shown, the address of the logo (null without one), the main color as
#RRGGBB (null for the color of the design system), the secondary color (null for none) and the address of the logo
for the dark theme (null without one, and the logo shows, ADR-0100). The address of a logo changes whenever the logo
changes, so the browser may keep it.

LinkCategoryCountResponse.description: A category the links of the project use, with how many links have it.

LinkCategoryResponse.description: A category of links: the name and whether it is active.

LinkListResponse.description:
The links found, the categories the links of the project use with how many each has, the total for the tab and
whether the person may include, change and remove links (false in a completed or cancelled project).

LinkRequest.description: A link as the person fills it in.

LinkResponse.description: A link of the project: the title, the address, what it is for, the category and who included it and when.

MessageColorsDto.description:
The colors of the messages of the tickets, one per part of the conversation, each #RRGGBB or null for the color of
the design system (ADR-0101).

MyWorkAcceptanceResponse.description: A request of acceptance of the queue: whether it is for the person, for whom, who asked, when and the milestone.

MyWorkAction.description: The one action of a line of the queue (ADR-0070, ADR-0096).

MyWorkGroup.description: The groups of the queue (ADR-0070), in the order of the screen.

MyWorkGroupResponse.description: A group of a view, with its items in order.

MyWorkItemResponse.description:
An item of the queue: the kind, the project, the title, the action of the line, the day it is due (none while it
waits for the person), the business days of delay, since when it waits for the person and what the kind tells.

MyWorkKind.description: What an item of the queue is: a ticket, a task of a schedule or a request of acceptance.

MyWorkPersonResponse.description: A person an item shows, by the current name.

MyWorkProjectResponse.description: The project of an item: the id and the code.

MyWorkResponse.description: Meu trabalho of the person: today and the next business day of the installation, and the three views.

MyWorkTaskResponse.description: A task of the queue: the phase and the progress.

MyWorkTicketResponse.description: A ticket of the queue: the number, the status, the team, who asked, who is in charge and which deadline counts.

MyWorkTicketStatus.description: The statuses of a ticket the queue shows: the open ones (ADR-0024).

MyWorkView.description: The views of Meu trabalho (ADR-0070), in the order of the screen.

MyWorkViewResponse.description: A view of the queue: how many items it has and the groups with items, in the order of the screen.

NewProjectMemberRequest.description:
The person to include, by `userId` or, for a person of the company directory who never signed in, by the
`directoryId` of the people search (ADR-0005), and the role in the project.

NewProjectRequest.description:
The new project: the code (as ERP-FIN, in any case), the name, the description and the client (none for an internal
project), the manager (the person who creates it, when none) and, optionally, the tech lead: a user or a person of
the company directory who never signed in, by the `directoryId` of the people search (ADR-0005). With a model, the
schedule is made from it, starting on `scheduleStart` (ADR-0017).

ownedByClient.description: The client of the project is in charge of the task, without an owner (ADR-0102).

NewScheduleItemRequest.description:
A new task or milestone: the kind, the phase, the name, the start, the duration in business days (zero or none for a
milestone), the owner (a person of the project who is not a viewer; none for a milestone), the progress from 0 to
100 (zero for a milestone), the items it depends on, and the task it goes into, right in the same phase (none for
right in the phase). The first subtask of a task takes the dependencies of the task (ADR-0088).

NewTemplateRequest.description: A new model from a schedule: its name and, optionally, its description.

NewTicketRequest.description:
A new ticket: the project, the team, the priority, the title and the description, without an assignee (ADR-0068). The
description comes with its formatting in `descriptionBody` (the JSON of the editor) or as plain text.

NoticeKind.description: What happened, for the notices (ADR-0037, ADR-0038): one kind per event of the table of ADR-0037.

NotificationPageResponse.description: A page of the bell, the newest first, with how many are not read and whether there are older ones.

NotificationResponse.description:
A notification of the bell (ADR-0038): what happened, the current name of who did it (null for the system), the
address of the item, its data (codes as the names of the enums, days as yyyy-MM-dd), when it arrived and whether it
was read.

OutboxEmailStatus.description: Where an e-mail of the queue stands (ADR-0036).

OverviewAcceptanceResponse.description: A pending request of acceptance the person sees.

OverviewAttentionResponse.description: What needs attention (ADR-0073), in the order of the list.

OverviewDeadlineResponse.description: The end of the schedule and, with a baseline, its end and the business days of deviation.

OverviewLateTaskResponse.description: A late task: its owner, progress, end, business days of delay and what depends on it.

OverviewMilestoneResponse.description: The next milestone not reached: its day, the business days left, or the business days it is late.

OverviewPersonResponse.description: A person of the overview, by the current name.

OverviewProgressResponse.description: The progress of the project and how much should be done by today (null with no task to plan), and by what.

OverviewRowKind.description: What a line of the timeline of the overview is.

OverviewRowResponse.description: A phase or a milestone of the smaller timeline (ADR-0071).

OverviewTeam.description: The teams of a project (ADR-0040, ADR-0068).

OverviewTeamResponse.description: A team of the project with its people and, for the teams that serve tickets, the open tickets.

OverviewTicketResponse.description: A ticket that needs attention: late, due up to the next business day or without an assignee.

OverviewTicketsResponse.description: The tickets of the project: the open ones of all, the late ones and the ones waiting for the requester.

OverviewTimelineResponse.description: The period of the schedule, its non-business days and its phases and milestones in order.

OverviewVendorTicketResponse.description: A ticket at a vendor without an update for the business days of the setting (ADR-0028).

PersonResponse.description:
A person to choose, such as the manager of a project or a person to include in it: a user (`id`) or a person of
the company directory who never signed in (`directoryId`), who becomes a user when included (ADR-0005). Only an
active Administrator or Project manager can be a manager (ADR-0085), and only an active Administrator or Tech lead a
tech lead (ADR-0097).

ProfileResponse.description:
My profile: who the person is, how they sign in, the theme they chose and whether they receive the daily summary of
e-mails. Sign-in providers come as their codes ("local", and "entra" later); the screen says them in words.

ProjectClientResponse.description: The client of a project, with the address of its current logo (null without one).

ProjectClosingResponse.description:
What completing or cancelling the project would leave behind (ADR-0043): the tickets not closed, which keep it from
being completed and are closed by the cancellation, and the tasks below 100% and the requests of acceptance waiting
for the answer, warnings.

ProjectListItemResponse.description: One project of the list; without a client, it is an internal project; without tasks and milestones, no schedule.

ProjectMemberCreatedResponse.description: The user now in the project; a person of the directory got this user when included.

ProjectMemberResponse.description:
A person of a project as the Members tab shows it: the e-mail, the role, when the person joined, the last sign-in
(null for who never signed in) and whether the person may be a manager (ADR-0085) or a tech lead (ADR-0097) of a project.

ProjectOverviewResponse.description:
The overview of a project (ADR-0073): today, the progress, the final deadline and the next milestone (null without a
schedule), the tickets, the timeline, what needs attention and the team.

ProjectPageResponse.description: A page of the list, with today in the time zone of the installation, the day the schedules are seen on.

ProjectPermissionsResponse.description:
What the person may do in the project (ADR-0043): change the data, only while the project is open; change the
status, including reopening it; and, while the project is open, include, change and remove people, do it also with
the managers (ADR-0042), and change the schedule.

ProjectPersonResponse.description: A person in a project, with the role in it.

ProjectRequest.description: The data of a project that may change after its creation.

ProjectResponse.description:
A project as its page shows it, with the people in it, what the person may do and the dates of the schedule (none
without tasks and milestones).

ProjectRole.description: The role of a person in one project (ADR-0040): one per person in each project.

ProjectScheduleSummaryResponse.description:
The schedule of a project in the list (ADR-0071): its dates, its progress, how many tasks and milestones are late
(ADR-0086), the current phase (the first late one or, without delays, the last that has started; none before the
start), the day the last task was completed when all are at 100%, the phases with items, the days of the
milestones and the business days of delay of the most late task or milestone (ADR-0096).

ProjectSituation.description: Which projects the list shows: the open ones, the closed ones (completed or cancelled) or all.

ProjectStatus.description: Where a project is in its life (ADR-0016). Completed and cancelled projects are closed.

ProjectTicketTeam.description: The team of a ticket (ADR-0068), as the overview of a project shows it.

ScheduleAction.description: The kind of a change of the schedule, for the screen to say what undoing or redoing it does (ADR-0091).

ScheduleBaselineResponse.description:
The baseline of the project (ADR-0021): the day it was saved, the start and the end of the project then, and the
business days the end of the project now is after (positive) or before (negative) it, null without items now.

ScheduleItemChangedResponse.description: How many items after the changed one were pushed later (ADR-0019).

ScheduleItemDatesRequest.description:
New dates from the timeline: the start alone keeps the duration; with the end, a task lasts the business days
between them. A milestone has no end.

ScheduleItemKind.description: A task has a start and a duration in business days; a milestone is one day, without duration (ADR-0018).

ownedByClient.description: The client of the project is in charge of the task, without an owner (ADR-0102).

ScheduleItemRequest.description:
A change of a task or a milestone, whose kind stays; without the progress, it stays as it is. Without the task it is
in, it goes right in the phase. A task with subtasks changes only its phase, name and owner: its start and duration
are not looked at, and it has no dependencies (ADR-0088).

ownedByClient.description: The client of the project is in charge of the task (ADR-0102).

ScheduleItemResponse.description:
A task or a milestone: the dates in business days of the calendar of the installation, the duration (zero for a
milestone), the progress (zero for a milestone), the day a task reached 100% or a milestone was reached, whether it
is late and by how many business days (from the day after the end up to today; for a task with subtasks, the most
of its subtasks; zero when it is not late, and while the delay began on non-business days only), whether the person
may update its progress now (only a task without subtasks, while the project is open), the owner, the ids of the
items it depends on, the task it is in and whether it has subtasks, whose dates and progress it then shows
(ADR-0088), whether it is on the critical path (never a task with subtasks), and its start and end in the baseline
with the business days its end is after (positive) or before (negative) them, all null when it was not in the
baseline (ADR-0021).

ScheduleItemType.description: What an item of a schedule is: a phase, a task (also a subtask) or a milestone.

ScheduleOwnerResponse.description: The person in charge of a task.

SchedulePhaseResponse.description:
A phase, with its dates (none without items), its progress weighted by duration and its items in order, each task
followed by its subtasks.

SchedulePhaseSummaryResponse.description: A phase in the strip of phases: its dates, its progress and whether a task or a milestone of it is late.

ScheduleProgressRequest.description: The progress of a task, from 0 to 100.

ScheduleResponse.description:
The schedule of a project on the day `today` of the installation: its dates (none without items), its progress,
how many tasks and milestones are late, the phases in order, the non-business days of the calendar from the month
before the start to the month after the end, for the timeline to shade (none without items), the baseline, none
until the manager saves one, and, for who edits the schedule, what undoing and redoing would do, none when nothing.

ScheduleStepResponse.description:
A change of the schedule the person made (ADR-0091): its kind and the name of the phase or item, as what undoing or
redoing does, or did.

SessionUserResponse.description: The person in the session, with the role in the system and the theme of their screens.

SignInOptionsResponse.description: How the sign-in page may sign people in.

SpreadsheetResponse.description: The spreadsheet read: the names of the sheets, the sheet read, the header and the lines under it.

SpreadsheetRowResponse.description: A line of the spreadsheet: its number in the spreadsheet and the text of each column.

SystemRole.description:
Role of a person in the whole system (ADR-0040). The numbering starts at 1, so an unset value is never a
valid role.

TemplateItemResponse.description:
A task or milestone of a model: its kind, name, duration in business days, how many business days after the start
it starts, and whether it is a subtask.

TemplatePhaseResponse.description: A phase of a model with its items in order.

TemplateRequest.description: The name, the description and the situation of a model.

TemplateResponse.description: A model of project: its name, description and situation, and its phases with their items (ADR-0017).

ThemePreference.description: The theme a person chose in the profile (ADR-0014); Automatic follows the operating system.

TicketAction.description: The actions of the flow of a ticket (ADR-0024), named in English in the table.

TicketActionResponse.description: An action of the flow the person may take now: where it leads and whether it needs a message (ADR-0024).

TicketActors.description: Who may take an action of the flow (ADR-0024, ADR-0044); a transition takes several.

TicketAssigneeRequest.description: A new assignee for the tickets, one or many (ADR-0027, ADR-0068).

TicketAttachmentResponse.description: An attachment of a ticket: of a message, or of the description when the message is null.

TicketConversationPermissionsResponse.description: What the person may do in the conversation, with the actions of the flow open now and the priority.

TicketCountsResponse.description:
How many tickets each list has: all of them, any status, and the open ones, the open ones without an assignee,
without an assignee in the teams of the person, in charge of the person, opened by the person, followed by the person
and with a ticket at a vendor.

TicketDeadlineSettingRequest.description: The deadlines of a priority to save, from 1 to 365 business days.

TicketDeadlineSettingResponse.description: The deadlines of a priority, in business days (ADR-0025).

TicketDeadlinesRequest.description: The deadlines of the four priorities, all at once.

oneOf.description: Null for a ticket closed without being resolved, as a cancelled one.

TicketDeadlinesResponse.description:
The deadlines of a ticket today (ADR-0025): the first answer (null once the ticket finished without one) and when it
was given, the resolution, the business days used of the total and the business days it waited for the requester.

TicketDueResponse.description: Where a deadline stands (ADR-0025): its state, the day it is due and, when overdue, by how many business days.

TicketDueState.description: Where a deadline stands today (ADR-0025), for the icon, the color and the text (ADR-0065).

TicketEventKind.description: What happened in a ticket besides the messages (ADR-0069): a change of status or the assignee set.

fromPersonId.description: The requester before, or the assignee who left.

vendorTicketId.description: The ticket at a vendor registered or updated, among the vendorTickets of the ticket.

note.description: The note of the update at the vendor.

TicketEventResponse.description:
An event of the conversation (ADR-0069): a change of status, with the action, or the assignee set; the actor is
null when the system did it.

TicketFlowResponse.description:
The flow of the tickets, read from its table, with the statuses in their order and after how many business days a
resolved ticket without an answer closes.

interactions.description: How many messages and events the ticket has.

oneOf.description: The deadline of the resolution today (ADR-0025); null for a ticket opened before the deadlines.

canChangeAssignee.description: The person may change the assignee, also with others at once (ADR-0068).

canChangeRequester.description: The person may change the requester with others at once (ADR-0027).

oneOf.description: The ticket at a vendor: the open one registered last, or the last one (ADR-0028); null without one.

TicketListItemResponse.description: A ticket of a list; without an assignee until someone of the team answers it (ADR-0068).

TicketMessageResponse.description: A message of the conversation, with its text as the JSON of the editor.

TicketParticipantResponse.description: A person of the conversation and the part the person plays in the ticket, for the color and the tag (ADR-0069).

TicketParticipantRole.description:
The part a person plays in a ticket, which gives the color and the tag of the messages (ADR-0069): the requester,
the assignee (even being of a team), the manager, the tech lead, the teams, the Administrator outside the project,
or anyone else.

TicketPriority.description: How urgent a ticket is, from the lowest to the highest.

TicketPriorityRequest.description: A new priority for the ticket.

TicketProjectChoiceResponse.description:
A project the person sees, for the filters and the opening: whether it is closed, whether the person may open
tickets in it and the teams with someone to serve them (ADR-0068).

TicketProjectResponse.description: The project of a ticket: the screens show the code beside the number (ADR-0029).

TicketRequesterRequest.description: A new requester for the tickets, one or many (ADR-0027).

descriptionBody.description: The description with its formatting, as the JSON of the editor; null for one written as plain text.

TicketResponse.description:
A ticket as its page shows it, with the people: the requester, the assignee, the managers and the tech leads of the
project; and its conversation (ADR-0026, ADR-0069): the messages, the attachments, who follows it, who may be
mentioned, the parts of the people who appear in it and what the person may do.

TicketSituation.description: Which tickets a list shows by status: the ones still in progress, the resolved and closed ones, or all.

TicketSort.description: The order of a list: by the priority, the highest first and the oldest first in each, or by the number.

TicketStatus.description: The status of a ticket (ADR-0024). A ticket is opened as Open; the flow between them comes from a table.

TicketTeam.description: The team a ticket goes to (ADR-0068): only these two, without queues.

TicketTeamRequest.description: The other team for the ticket (ADR-0068).

body.description: The message, as the JSON of the editor, without mentions; needed by the actions that ask for one.

TicketTransitionRequest.description: An action of the flow taken in a ticket, with the message when the action needs one.

actors.description: Attendant, Requester, Manager, Administrator or System.

automatic.description: Taken by the system on its own, never offered as a button.

TicketTransitionResponse.description: A transition of the flow (ADR-0024): from a status to another by an action, who may take it, and how.

TicketVendorResponse.description: A ticket at a vendor as a list shows it, with the business days without an update once it is stale.

UnreadNotificationsResponse.description: How many notifications of the person are not read.

UpcomingMilestoneProjectResponse.description: The project of a milestone ahead.

UpcomingMilestoneResponse.description:
A milestone ahead of the projects of the person: the day, the business days left until it (none on the day itself)
and whether a request of acceptance for it waits for the answer.

UpcomingMilestonesResponse.description: The milestones ahead, the soonest first, and today in the time zone of the installation.

oneOf.description: The colors of the messages of the tickets; null keeps none, the design system's.

UpdateInstallationRequest.description:
The General settings form, saved as a whole: the name shown, the IANA time zone, the main color (#RRGGBB, or null
for the color of the design system), the time of the daily summary (HH:mm:ss, in the time zone), how many days the
notifications are kept (1 to 365) and the secondary color (#RRGGBB, or null for none, ADR-0100).

UserResponse.description: One person on the Users screen.

VendorRequest.description: The name, the portal and the situation of a vendor.

VendorResponse.description: A vendor of the installation (ADR-0028): its name, the address of its support portal and its situation.

VendorTicketRequest.description: A ticket opened at an active vendor to register in our ticket.

staleDays.description: The business days without an update, once it reaches the setting of the installation; null otherwise.

VendorTicketResponse.description:
A ticket opened at a vendor and registered in our ticket (ADR-0028): the vendor, its number and the day it was opened
there, the status there, the link, the note, who registered it and when it was last updated, with the business days
without an update once it is stale.

VendorTicketStatus.description: Where a ticket stands at the vendor (ADR-0028); the vendor decides its own cycle, so any status follows any other.

VendorTicketUpdateRequest.description: The new status of a ticket at a vendor, with a note.

WorkingDaysRequest.description: The days of the week the installation works; at least one.
